metadata.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis (Mildenhall et al., 2020)
metadata.framework: Continuous volumetric scene representation via MLP mapping 5D coordinates to radiance and density, trained with differentiable volume rendering
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:2003.08934.

nodes.name: Neural radiance field representation
nodes.statement: A neural radiance field is a continuous function $F_\Theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \to (\mathbf{c}, \sigma)$ represented by an MLP with weights $\Theta$. It maps a 3D location $\mathbf{x} = (x, y, z)$ and 2D viewing direction $\mathbf{d} = (\theta, \phi)$ to an emitted color $\mathbf{c} = (r, g, b)$ and a volume density $\sigma$. The density $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ depends only on location (view-independent), while color $\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ depends on both location and direction (view-dependent appearance).

nodes.name: Volume rendering equation
nodes.statement: The expected color $C(\mathbf{r})$ of camera ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$ with near and far bounds $t_n, t_f$ is $C(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{t_n}^{t_f} T(t) \sigma(\mathbf{r}(t)) \mathbf{c}(\mathbf{r}(t), \mathbf{d}) \, dt$, where $T(t) = \exp\left(-\int_{t_n}^{t} \sigma(\mathbf{r}(s)) \, ds\right)$ is the accumulated transmittance along the ray from $t_n$ to $t$.

nodes.name: Discretized volume rendering (quadrature)
nodes.statement: The continuous integral is approximated by stratified sampling: partition $[t_n, t_f]$ into $N$ bins, sample $t_i \sim \mathcal{U}[t_n + \frac{i-1}{N}(t_f - t_n), \, t_n + \frac{i}{N}(t_f - t_n)]$, and compute $\hat{C}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} T_i (1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)) \mathbf{c}_i$, where $T_i = \exp\left(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j\right)$ and $\delta_i = t_{i+1} - t_i$. This is differentiable with respect to the MLP parameters.

nodes.name: Positional encoding
nodes.statement: To enable the MLP to represent high-frequency scene content, each input coordinate $p$ is mapped via $\gamma(p) = (\sin(2^0 \pi p), \cos(2^0 \pi p), \ldots, \sin(2^{L-1} \pi p), \cos(2^{L-1} \pi p))$. For 3D position, $L = 10$ (60 components); for viewing direction, $L = 4$ (24 components). Without positional encoding, the MLP produces oversmoothed results due to spectral bias toward low frequencies.

nodes.name: Hierarchical volume sampling (coarse-to-fine)
nodes.statement: Two networks are trained: a 'coarse' network and a 'fine' network. The coarse network is evaluated at $N_c$ stratified samples. Its output weights $w_i = T_i(1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i))$ define a piecewise-constant PDF along the ray, from which $N_f$ additional samples are drawn via inverse CDF sampling. The fine network is evaluated at the union of $N_c + N_f$ samples, concentrating computation near visible surfaces.

nodes.name: NeRF MLP architecture
nodes.statement: The MLP has 8 fully-connected layers (256 channels each) with ReLU activations. The positionally-encoded position is input to the first layer, with a skip connection concatenating it again at the 5th layer. After 8 layers, the network outputs $\sigma$ and a 256-d feature, which is concatenated with the encoded viewing direction and passed through one additional layer to produce the RGB color $\mathbf{c}$.

nodes.name: NeRF optimization procedure
nodes.statement: The loss is $\mathcal{L} = \sum_{\mathbf{r} \in \mathcal{R}} \left[ \|\hat{C}_c(\mathbf{r}) - C(\mathbf{r})\|_2^2 + \|\hat{C}_f(\mathbf{r}) - C(\mathbf{r})\|_2^2 \right]$, summing over a batch $\mathcal{R}$ of rays, with $\hat{C}_c$ and $\hat{C}_f$ from the coarse and fine networks respectively, and $C(\mathbf{r})$ the ground-truth pixel color. Optimized with Adam ($5 \times 10^{-4}$ learning rate, exponentially decayed). One scene takes ~100-300k iterations on a single GPU.

nodes.name: View synthesis results
nodes.statement: NeRF achieves state-of-the-art novel view synthesis on synthetic (Blender) and real (LLFF) datasets, with PSNR improvements of 3-5 dB over prior methods (SRN, LLFF, Neural Volumes). Qualitative results show sharp edges, fine detail, and consistent view-dependent effects (reflections, specularities) that prior methods fail to capture.

nodes.name: Ablation: positional encoding and hierarchical sampling
nodes.statement: Removing positional encoding reduces PSNR by ~4 dB (oversmoothed results). Removing view dependence reduces PSNR by ~1 dB (cannot model specularities). Removing hierarchical sampling reduces quality and increases noise. Each component contributes significantly to final quality.
